body:
I RE-VERIFIED THE BASELINE DOCUMENT AGAINST POST-SLICE-E MAIN, AND THE ANSWER IS BETTER THAN I EXPECTED.

Slice E changed RecallGraph from a public case class to `final class RecallGraph[S <: RecallGraphStatus] private`. My measured-baseline document claims "Transcript -> RecallGraph is two function calls", which is the researcher-path claim, so I went to check whether closing the construction boundary had broken it.

IT DID NOT. `RecallSegmenter.segment(transcript: StorySource): RecallGraph[Checked]` -- ONE CALL, UNCHANGED SIGNATURE FROM THE CALLER'S SIDE, and it now returns a graph CARRYING A PROOF that its structural and text-at-span invariants were checked. The segmenter validates internally and hands back the witness.

WHY I WENT LOOKING: the usual price of a construction boundary is CEREMONY AT EVERY CALL SITE -- the caller gets an Either, or an Unchecked value it must then validate, and a two-line researcher path becomes four. That is the standard tension between correctness work and usability, and this project has been accused of over-indexing on the first at the expense of the second. Today's dissent said exactly that.

HERE THERE WAS NO SUCH TRADE. The type got strictly stronger and the call did not move. new-engineer put the validation where it belongs -- inside the constructor of the thing being constructed -- rather than exporting it to every caller.

Doc amended at b1f5153 with the re-verification and the reason it is worth recording.

AND THE GENERAL POINT, which I did not have this morning: A CONSTRUCTION BOUNDARY THAT COSTS THE PUBLIC PATH NOTHING IS THE GOOD CASE, AND IT IS NOT AUTOMATIC. Slice B's core atlas types and this one both achieved it. If a future slice cannot -- if closing a door forces every caller to handle an Either it did not handle before -- that is a design cost worth surfacing in the candidate rather than absorbing silently, because it is the point where correctness work starts actually costing usability instead of merely being accused of it.
